items.title: Why Netflix Stock Is At A One-Year Low
items.summary: Our Nov 16 piece, Can Netflix Stock Fall 50%, found that Netflix (NFLX) has fallen 50% or more from high to low in three of the 15 market shocks it has traded through. That is the crash question. The next question is the one owners live with every day: what is the real risk now, with no shock in sight.

items.title: 3 Undervalued Stocks Trading Up To 47% Below Fair Value
items.summary: AI chip exports to China now face tighter US controls, which has pushed investors to rethink what they pay for future growth stories. Cash rich businesses trading below estimated fair value can suddenly look a lot more interesting than crowded momentum trades. This article walks through three stocks that screen as potentially mispriced on their cash flows and shows where disciplined buyers might see opportunity. items.title: NFLX Stock Edges Higher Overnight: Evercore Swaps Netflix For Spotify On Top Picks List
items.summary: Evercore ISI noted that Spotify’s stock had recently rallied 30%, making it a better pick than Netflix, which is currently trading within 10% of its three-year lows.

items.title: Netflix Stock Now Trades at a 70% Discount to Its Peak Valuation, and One Number Is to Blame
items.summary: Market sentiment has taken a negative turn for a business investors considered a perennial winner.

items.title: Netflix Lowers 2026 Ad Revenue Forecast: Time to Hold the Stock?
items.summary: NFLX cuts its 2026 ad revenue forecast to $2.7B, but strong margins, cash flow and a packed content slate support holding the stock despite valuation risks.

items.title: US High Relative Profitability (DUHP) Buys $69.9 Million More Broadcom on Nov. 12
items.summary: The fund added $444.6 million in net new positions, led by a $69.9 million purchase of Broadcom, while selling $9.3 million of Meta Platforms.

items.title: ETFs Are Buying Netflix (NFLX) on Nov. 12
items.summary: ETFs bought $59.6 million of Netflix stock, with 42 funds buying and 12 selling.

items.title: Trump Backs a Hollywood Tax Break So Movies “Must Stay in America.” Netflix and Disney Could Gain
items.summary: Key TakeawaysPresident Trump backed a bipartisan bill that would give US film and TV productions a 20% federal tax credit on labor costs. A credit would lower what Netflix and Disney pay to film in the US, helping cash flow and margins.
